firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hi everyone! 👋

As part of our submission to the **Google – The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track** (*"Why Local Coding Agents Get Stuck: A Diagnostic Benchmark and Counterfactual Context-Reset Protocol for Quantized Gemma 4"* — official Hackathon Writeup submitted; unlocks publicly on Kaggle after the Nov 13 deadline), we are open-sourcing our complete **Trap-25 Diagnostic Benchmark**, **LoopBreakerEngine**, and **Verification Notebook** for the community today!

- 📊 **Public Dataset (10.00 Usability — `trap_tasks_25.jsonl` + `LoopBreakerEngine` + Telemetry CSVs):** [Gemma 4 Loop-Breaker & Trap-25 Benchmark](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/robinamirbahar/gemma-4-loop-breaker-and-trap-25-benchmark)
- 💻 **Public Executable Verification Notebook:** [Gemma 4 Loop-Breaker: CCR & Trap-25 Benchmark](https://www.kaggle.com/code/robinamirbahar/gemma-4-loop-breaker-ccr-trap-25-benchmark)
- 🏆 **Paper Track Competition:** [Google – The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent-paper)

---

### Why Local Coding Agents Hit "The 15-Minute Cliff"
When a quantized `gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct` or `gemma-4-12b-it-qat-w4a16-ct` agent applies a plausible first-guess patch that fails an edge-case `pytest` assertion, raw stack traces and failed `git diff` blocks accumulate in the `w4a16-ct` KV cache. Under low-temperature decoding (`temp = 0.20 - 0.35`), attention weight over the original issue specification decays while recent error tokens dominate, trapping the agent in A-B-A edit loops.

![4-Arm Ablation Results on the Gemma 4 Trap-25 Benchmark](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F19770680%2F49e178a301e17188a517d4218a430a9e%2Ffig2_ablation_comparison.png?generation=1792601324860823&alt=media)

### Key Findings from Our 4-Arm Ablation (100 Multi-Turn Trajectories):
1. **Static Unpruned Baseline (`baseline_static`):** Resolves **16.0% (4/25)** of trap tasks (`158,880` cumulative KV tokens; `45,220` `<|think|>` tokens).
2. **Naive Sub-Agent Handoff (`naive_subagent`):** Adding a prompt-only analyzer sub-agent every 3 turns without KV-cache pruning resolves **20.0% (5/25)** while inflating KV tokens by **+19.3%** (`189,517` tokens) and `<|think|>` tokens by **+13.0%** (`51,118` tokens).
3. **Counterfactual Context Reset Only (`ccr_only`):** Monitoring 3 trajectory signals (Consecutive Error-Signature Persistence $C_{\text{err}} \ge 2$, Diff Similarity $S_{\text{diff}} \ge 0.82$, and Action Entropy $H_W < 0.55\text{ bits}$), pruning polluted middle turns, and injecting a compact `~150 token` `<NEGATIVE_CONSTRAINT_LEDGER>` jumps resolution to **72.0% (18/25)** (`-46.8%` KV tokens).
4. **CCR + Phase-Adaptive Thinking (`ccr_adaptive_ours`):** Throttling `<|think|>` tokens by **87.5%** (`4096 -> 512` tokens) during routine file reads and bursting to `6144` `<|think|>` tokens at `temp = 0.75` immediately after a reset reaches **96.0% (24/25)** resolution while cutting cumulative KV tokens by **70.8%** (`46,367` tokens) and `<|think|>` tokens by **45.1%** (`24,842` tokens).

![Sawtooth KV-Cache Trajectory Across 12 Turns](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F19770680%2Fff2cc79b337dad3f84a4039f0fe76247%2Ffig3_kv_cache_sawtooth_curve.png?generation=1792601360213385&alt=media)

![Domain-Wise Task Resolution Rate Across All 5 Python Domains](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F19770680%2F4c2de61a027e48786e7d18204a797be3%2Ffig4_domain_heatmap.png?generation=1792601380756291&alt=media)

All 25 3-state tasks (`buggy_code`, `trap_patch`, `gold_patch`, `test_code`) across `httpx`, `requests`, `fastapi`, `rich`, and `sci_compute` execute in < 10 seconds in standard Python `unittest`/`pytest` with zero external dependencies.

If you find the benchmark or CCR protocol useful for your agents, an upvote on the [Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/robinamirbahar/gemma-4-loop-breaker-and-trap-25-benchmark) and [Notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/robinamirbahar/gemma-4-loop-breaker-ccr-trap-25-benchmark) is greatly appreciated—and questions or feedback are very welcome!
